payload.body: Harmonicity is a human-made audio analysis feature that quantifies how closely a signal's spectral content matches a periodic (harmonic) model versus a noise-like model. It is computed by comparing the energy of spectral peaks that align with a harmonic template (partials at integer multiples of a fundamental frequency f0) to the residual energy that falls between those partials. Parameters: (1) a fundamental frequency estimate f0, (2) the number of harmonic partials to consider, (3) a tolerance window around each partial bin, (4) the power spectrum from which energy is measured. The persistence mechanism is the ratio H = E_harmonic / (E_harmonic + E_residual), yielding a value in [0, 1], where 1 indicates perfect harmonicity and 0 indicates pure noise. [formal: harmonicitas | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Spectral-band-asymmetry is a statistical descriptor quantifying how unevenly spectral energy is distributed across the frequency bins within a defined sub-band. Parameters: (1) lower and upper frequency bounds of the sub-band, (2) the energy values per frequency bin within the band. Computed as the normalized sum of absolute deviations from the band centroid: A = sum_i(|f_i - f_c| * E_i) / sum_i(E_i), where f_i is the frequency of bin i, f_c is the band centroid (weighted mean frequency), and E_i is the energy in bin i. The value is expressed in Hertz and indicates the spatial spread of energy around the centroid — higher values mean energy is concentrated toward one edge of the band, lower values mean energy is more centrally distributed. Persistence mechanism: arithmetic computation over the finite set of per-bin energy values for the given band and analysis frame. [formal: asymmetria spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Spectral-peak-trough-ratio is a human-made spectral feature quantifying the contrast between dominant spectral peaks and the valleys between them within a defined frequency range. It is computed by first identifying local maxima (peaks) and minima (troughs) in the magnitude spectrum, then calculating the ratio of mean peak energy to mean trough energy: PTR = mean(E_peak) / mean(E_trough). Parameters: (1) a frequency range or band over which to compute the ratio, (2) a minimum peak height threshold to distinguish true peaks from noise, (3) a minimum distance between adjacent peaks. Values greater than 1 indicate a spectrum with prominent peaks above the trough floor; higher values indicate sharper, more tonal spectra. Persistence mechanism: computed numerically from discrete magnitude spectra, stored as a scalar value per analysis frame. [formal: ratio culminis et vallis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Spectral-band-band-center is a spectral analysis parameter representing the geometric mean center frequency of spectral energy within a defined frequency sub-band. Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds, (2) the spectral energy values across frequency bins within the band. Computed as the geometric mean: exp(sum(f_i * ln(E_i)) / sum(E_i)) where f_i is the frequency of bin i and E_i is the spectral energy at that bin — distinct from spectral-band-centroid's arithmetic weighted mean. Values approach the geometric center of the energy distribution, which is lower than the arithmetic centroid when the distribution is right-skewed. Persistence mechanism: arithmetic computation over per-bin energy values for a given band and analysis frame, displayed as a scalar time series. [formal: centrum geometricum fasciae | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Built to persist through audio coding, music information retrieval, and acoustic analysis systems.

payload.body: Spectral-band-peak-trough-ratio is a human-made spectral analysis parameter quantifying the ratio between the mean energy of spectral peaks and the mean energy of troughs within a defined frequency sub-band. It is computed by: (1) identifying local maxima (peaks) and minima (troughs) in the per-bin energy vector restricted to the band's frequency range [f_low, f_high), (2) calculating the ratio of mean peak energy to mean trough energy: BTR = mean(E_peak) / mean(E_trough). Parameters: (1) the band's lower and upper frequency bounds (f_low, f_high), (2) the per-bin energy vector within those bounds, (3) a minimum peak height threshold to distinguish true peaks from noise, (4) a minimum distance between adjacent peaks. Values greater than 1 indicate a spectrum with prominent peaks above the trough floor; higher values indicate sharper, more tonal spectral content within the band. Persistence mechanism: computed numerically from discrete per-bin energy vectors over analysis frames, stored as a scalar time series. [formal: ratio culminis et vallis fasciae | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.scope: A human-made signal processing construct: a quantifiable property extracted from the time-domain representation of an audio signal that captures a specific characteristic useful for analysis, classification, or retrieval.

payload.name: temporal-feature
payload.scope: A human-made signal processing construct: a quantifiable property extracted from the time-domain representation of an audio signal that captures a specific characteristic useful for analysis, classification, or retrieval.

payload.body: A temporal-feature is a numerical descriptor extracted from the time-domain representation (waveform, energy envelope, or amplitude modulation) of an audio signal that captures a measurable aspect of its temporal structure. The n-th moment of the energy envelope, the rate of sign changes in the signal, and the time to reach peak energy are canonical instances. Parameters: (1) the temporal domain source — the discrete-time waveform, the short-time energy envelope, or the amplitude modulation envelope from which the feature is computed; (2) the computation — the specific mathematical operation applied (e.g., weighted mean of time indices for centroid, count of sign transitions for zero-crossing rate, first threshold-crossing time for attack); (3) dimensionality — whether the result is a single scalar, a time series, or a binary flag. Persistence mechanism: standardized mathematical definitions used across audio analysis, music information retrieval, and speech processing toolkits (librosa, Essentia, HTK, Praat) and encoded in published feature extraction pipelines. [formal: characteristicum temporale | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Sense: temporal-feature as a category of descriptors extracted from the time-domain representation of audio signals. This files against audio-feature — the established category for quantifiable properties extracted from audio signals. The temporal domain is orthogonal to the spectral domain: spectral-feature covers frequency-domain descriptors while temporal-feature covers time-domain descriptors. Both reduce signal content to numeric descriptors useful for analysis and classification. This is not a leap: temporal-feature is the nearest accepted kind.

payload.name: energy-envelope
payload.scope: A human-made audio representation: the per-frame time series of a signal's energy, obtained from a discrete-time waveform by windowing and magnitude squaring.

payload.name: energy-envelope
payload.scope: A human-made audio representation: the per-frame time series of a signal's energy, obtained from a discrete-time waveform by windowing and magnitude squaring.

payload.body: The energy-envelope is the per-frame time series of a signal's energy, a human-made representation derived from a discrete-time waveform by framing, windowing, and magnitude squaring. Parameters: (1) the analysis frame length (typically 20-40 ms), (2) the hop between successive frames, (3) the window function applied within each frame (e.g. Hamming, Hanning), and (4) the squaring convention - raw x^2(t), windowed |w(t) x(t)|^2, or the per-frame sum that projects to short-time-energy as its scalar value. Distinction: it is the energy series, not the per-frame scalar (short-time-energy) and not the per-sample Hilbert amplitude (amplitude-envelope); it is the operand on which temporal-centroid (first moment of the energy envelope) and onset-related energy readings operate. Persistence mechanism: standardized windowed computation across audio analysis and speech toolkits (librosa, Essentia, HTK, Praat), encoded in published feature-extraction pipelines. [formal: envelopium energiae | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
